advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider adding an upper version bound (e.g. `git-remote-s3>=0.3.2,<1`) to constrain future breaking releases of the S3 remote helper.
evidence: src/rebar/_optional.py `minimum_version = (0, 3, 2)` — guard checks only a floor, accepting any newer version (test_edge_newer_version_succeeds uses 0.4.0)
`# helper (Apache-2.0) so `sync.remote` can point at an s3://bucket/prefix remote.`
ABSENCE: no license-check tooling or allowlist entry visible in the diff to enforce/verify the Apache-2.0 claim for the newly-added dependency
advisory.finding: The `git-remote-s3` dependency in pyproject.toml uses an open-ended lower bound (`>=0.3.2`) with no upper bound, so future (potentially breaking) major/minor releases of an external remote helper will be pulled in when operators install/upgrade the `[s3]` extra, and the runtime guard only enforces the floor, not a ceiling.
merged_from: The pyproject comment asserts git-remote-s3 is Apache-2.0 licensed, but there is no automated license verification or record; the claim is documented only in a hand-written comment.
scenarios: An operator installs the s3 extra after git-remote-s3 ships a breaking 1.x that changes the remote-helper protocol; resolution succeeds but behavior breaks.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add version fixtures with fewer than three numeric components (e.g. '0.3' expecting failure, '1' expecting success) to exercise the zero-padding branch.
evidence: Test versions used: '0.3.2','0.2.9','0.4.0','0.3.2.post1','unknown' — all have three numeric leading parts; no fixture with <3 numeric components (e.g. '0.3' or '1').
advisory.finding: The version zero-padding branch for versions with fewer than three components is untested. All version fixtures ('0.3.2', '0.2.9', '0.4.0', '0.3.2.post1', 'unknown') have three numeric leading parts; none exercises the `while len(parsed_version) < 3` padding at lines 154-156. A two-component version like '0.3' must pad to (0,3,0) and fail the >=0.3.2 floor, while '1' must pad to (1,0,0) and succeed — neither path is covered, so a regression in the padding/comparison for short versions would go undetected.
scenarios: A short version string like '0.3' regresses to being accepted instead of rejected against the 0.3.2 floor.
A short version like '1' regresses to being rejected despite meeting the minimum.

evidence: `dependencies = [ { name = "boto3" }, { name = "botocore" }, { name = "urllib3" } ]` under the new git-remote-s3 package
ABSENCE: no new [[package]] blocks for boto3/botocore/urllib3 appear in the diff, implying they were already locked
dropped.finding: The lockfile adds git-remote-s3's transitive dependencies (boto3, botocore, urllib3) as declared deps but does not introduce new [[package]] pins in this diff, so confirm these transitives are already pinned/hashed elsewhere in uv.lock and are covered by the s3 extra's resolution.
scenarios: If a transitive were not previously locked, the s3 extra could resolve to an unpinned transitive at install time.
